caption:
Most shops don't lose leads to bad service.

They lose them to a deadline nobody wrote down.

Ask any team if a five-minute reply matters and most say yes. Watch them on a busy day and most still miss the window.

Good intentions break down under real call volume. A written standard is what holds up when the phones don't stop.

Build yours this week:
1. Set the window (5 min for calls/texts, 15 for forms)
2. Name who owns it each shift
3. Automate the first message so the clock never starts blank

That last step is what a missed-call text-back does. The moment a call goes unanswered, your number replies on its own. The standard holds even when nobody's free.

See it running on your own number. 14 days, no card.

rationale: Reframes speed-to-lead around an operational cause, no written standard, rather than a numeric benchmark, so it stays useful and distinct from prior stat-led posts while tying directly to the missed-call text-back feature as the fix.
